newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF group sees French bonds backing euro future.
newsitem.headline: MATIF group sees French bonds backing euro future.

text.p: A working group set up by the futures and options exchange MATIF said it favoured a straight shift from French franc 10-year bond futures to 10-year euro futures, with only French government bonds eligible for delivery.
A report published on Wednesday by the group said "At this stage, the members of the working committee favour a single-issue contract, with the French government the only issuer."
The report outlined how the group thought MATIF should position itself to compete for euro business after the planned introduction of a single currency in 1999.

Whether bonds issued by other countries within the euro-zone would eventually be eligible for delivery into a MATIF euro contract depended on whether a significant yield spread persisted between the euro-denominated bonds, the group said.

"The question of enlarging the pool to include other issuers will obviously have to be re-examined as underlying markets evolve, the aim being to dispose at all times of a large homogenous pool," the report said.
It said there was a possibility the euro contract could eventually be based on a "multiple-issue pool made up of instruments carrying the EMU's top-grade signatures."
The homogeneity of the pool of government bonds would depend not only on the quality of the issuer but also on the degree of liquidity in the bond market, the report said.
The group said MATIF's 10-year Ecu contract could evolve into a 10-year multiple-issuer euro contract if its 10-year euro future were to remain based on a single issuer.
In that case, the current 10-year Ecu contract could well be based on "a pool of lower-quality instruments", the report said.
The committee also looked at a scenario under which implementation of a single currency was delayed or cancelled altogether.

"The measures to be taken in these circumstances differ depending on how long EMU (European Monetary Union) is postponed, the degree to which the new starting date can be foreseen, and the probability of a complete cancellation of EMU," it said.
